full_judgment: 4. Defendant Nos. 6, 9-10 contested the suit by filing written objection denying all the material statements made in the plaint Their case, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Sheikh Akbor, who died leaving two sons, namely, Fazar Ali and Misir Ali, one daughter, 'Omarjan and a widow Jamela Bibi. After that, Misir Ali died leaving' behind his mother, brother and sister and a daughter Fulbanu. After death of Jamela Bibi, her son, Fazar Ali and daughter Ornarjan inherited 33/40th share of the suit khatian and they amicably partitioned the ejmali land by a registered deed of partition dated 24.03.1939 and the land of suit plot Nos. 158 and 204 had entirely fallen in the saham of Fazar Ali. Thereafter, Fazar Ali died leaving behind wife, Gulbodon and two minor daughters and Gulbodon on her behalf and on behalf of her minor daughters transferred the suit land to Barkutullah Munshi by a: registered deed of sale dated, 13.09.1950. Barkatullah in his turn sold the same to Abdul All by a registered deed of sale dated 11.04.1951. Abdul Ali married Fulbanu, daughter of Misir Ali and defendant No. 1, Falan @ Falu Mia was born out of their wed-lock. Falu Mia (defendant No. 1), transferred 'the land of suit plots to defendant No. 2. by a registered deed, of sale dated 28.07.1979, to defendant Nos. 3 and 4 by a registered deed of sale dated 07.04.1979, to defendant No. 5 by a registered deed of sale dated 22.03.1979 and to the defendant-petitioners by a registered deed of sale dated 23.01.1980 The defendants were inducted into possession of the suit land and they got 'their names mutated in the khatian and have been in possession thereof. The plaintiff obtained ex parte decree in Title' Suit No. 153 of 1990 by practicing fraud and suppressing the summons of the suit. The plaintiff kidnapped defendant No. 1 on 06.12.1994 and' his son lodged a G. D. Entry being No 919 dated 22.01.1995 with Lalbagh Police Station to that effect. The plaintiff filed Miscellaneous, Case No. 15 of 1992 and Miscellaneous Appeal. No. 24,1 of 1995 by false personation in the names of defendants and those cases were dismissed for default at the instance of the plaintiff. The whereabouts of defendant No. 1 was not known to 'these defendants for about 5/6' 'years and his heirs could not be substituted in his place as the Court refused to declare his civil death. The suit is false and the same is liable to be dismissed.
